symptom: `drop microflow` + `create microflow` of an unchanged describe lost a parameter's documentation on a flow Studio Pro authored, but not on a copy mxcli had created. Reproduced on Administration.ChangePassword in a 10.24.11 and an 11.12.6 blank project after setting the parameter's Documentation in the stored unit.
file: modelsdk/canon/transplant.go alignSlices / pairLeftovers / lcsPairsPlaced; modelsdk/canon/translations.go carryTranslationsByID, samePlaces; modelsdk/canon/identity.go Reconcile. Test: modelsdk/canon/transplant_unordered_2329_test.go
cause: Studio Pro stores a flow's objects in drawing order; mxcli writes the parameters and the start event first. TransplantIDs aligned the list on the longest common run of activities, so the parameter and start event fell in a gap with nothing (or another $Type) opposite and got fresh $IDs; every carry keyed on $ID (unstatedFlowDefaults' parameter Documentation) then missed them. The same reorder let two show messages cross: the alignment by order paired each with the other.
insight: **`Objects` is a set stored as a list, so an ordered alignment is the wrong tool for it, and the position is the key a describe preserves.** Two changes to the alignment: entries left unpaired (or held by a positional pair of different $Types, which pairs nothing) pair by matchKey when it is unique among the leftovers on both sides; and the LCS scores a same-place match (RelativeMiddlePoint) 12 against 2, so same-place pairs win over a longer run of guesses and an insertion that moved everything aligns as before. The translation carry then gained a pass after the transplant keyed on the paired Texts$Text $ID, applied only when the pairing is confirmed (same owner place, or every written language agrees), and the existing by-path pass is refused when two texts at one path are owned by objects at different places. Measured: drop + create of all 16 stock 10.24.11 microflows kept 612 of 821 element ids before and 722 after; 0 mx check errors; a describe → create or modify of all 16 is still 'already in sync'. A live check is what found the crossing: changing one message's text in the drop + create carried the OTHER message's nl_NL onto it until the place broke the tie. The reporter's translation loss itself (10.24.11, four languages) did not reproduce on the stock project; the ambiguous-source and changed-source cases are what the by-$ID pass covers.
